transcript.text: Bosch HBS534BS0B oven displaying E011 and won't let me do anything. Beeping. Help!

That's annoying, but it's often fixable. A locked-out display that keeps beeping usually means the controls have stopped accepting input until the fault clears. I'll be honest about the code: sources disagree on what E011 means on Bosch ovens, so I can't confirm it for your model. I'll work from what the oven is doing instead. The most likely causes, in order: 1. A button or touch key being read as pressed or stuck. Steam, condensation, grease or something resting on the panel can cause this.
2. A temporary glitch in the electronics that a power reset will clear.
3. Less likely, a genuine internal fault such as a temperature sensor or the control module. That would need an engineer. Checks to try, simplest first: 1. Look at the control panel. Make sure nothing is leaning on or touching the buttons, such as a tea towel, a utensil or a child's hand. Then wipe the panel with a barely damp cloth and dry it thoroughly, especially around the buttons. If it was moisture or dirt, the code should stop.
2. Do a power reset. Switch the oven off at the cooker switch (the large wall switch near the oven), or at the cooker breaker in the fuse box. Leave it off for 2–3 minutes, then switch it back on. You may need to reset the clock afterwards. If E011 doesn't return, it was most likely a glitch or a key reading falsely.
3. If it comes back on, press each button once, firmly and separately. Check whether any feel stuck, spongy or different from the others. A key that doesn't spring back points to the control or touch panel.
4. Check whether a key or child lock symbol is lit. If so, the manual will show which button to hold to unlock it. If the code clears and stays away, keep an eye on it. If it returns straight after a reset, or comes back once the oven heats up, that points away from a simple key problem. It would suggest a fault in the control panel or a temperature-related part, and an engineer is the sensible next step. Bosch's own service can look up exactly what the code means for your model. What happens after the clean and the power reset?

Dried the panel with a towel and switched off at the cooker switch for 5 mins. It's come back up normally, no code. It heated to 180C fine too. There was a bit of spray residue along the bottom edge of the panel before I dried it.

Good news, it sounds sorted. The spray residue along the bottom edge of the panel is the most likely culprit. Touch controls can read moisture or a film of cleaner as a finger held on a key. The oven then locks out and beeps. Drying it and doing the reset cleared that, and it heating to 180C with no code returning is reassuring. To stop it happening again, spray cleaner onto the cloth rather than straight onto the oven front. Wipe the panel with the oven switched off, and dry it afterwards, especially along the bottom edge where drips collect. If E011 ever comes back with a clean, dry panel, or reappears once the oven is hot, that would point to a genuine panel or sensor fault. Then a Bosch engineer would be the next step. Is there anything else I can help with?

An electronic glitch in the controls that a power reset clears (medium)
An internal fault reported by the control electronics, such as a temperature sensor or control module problem (low)

plan: Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Bosch; model HBS534BS0B; code E011.
The fault they reported is: "error code shown, controls unresponsive, beeping". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.

Explain what the error code means using ERROR CODES. If ERROR CODES does not resolve it, say plainly that you cannot confirm what it means on their model (it may not be an error code at all, for example part of the model name), never guess a meaning, and work from the symptoms.
